column3: n. 超大陆
column5: Geologists believe a new supercontinent could form roughly two hundred million years from now.
column6: 地质学家认为,大约两亿年后可能会形成新的超级大陆。

column3: v. 掩饰, 假装, 装糊涂
column5: She could not dissimulate her surprise when the exam results were read out.
column6: 宣读考试成绩时,她无法掩饰自己的惊讶。

column3: a. 铁磁体;磁性铁的
column5: Iron and nickel are ferromagnetic materials that respond strongly to outside magnetic fields.
column6: 铁和镍是铁磁性材料,对外部磁场反应强烈。

column3: n. 工匠；手艺人；工艺师
column5: The fair brought together forty craftspeople selling pottery, leather goods, and handwoven textiles.
column6: 集市汇聚了四十位手艺人,售卖陶器、皮具和手织布。

column3: adv. 卓越地, 超群地
column5: The young cellist played with surpassingly delicate phrasing that silenced the whole hall.
column6: 年轻大提琴手的乐句处理格外细腻,全场为之屏息。

column3: v. 咀嚼
column5: Dietitians remind children to masticate each mouthful thoroughly before swallowing.
column6: 营养师提醒孩子们每一口食物都要充分咀嚼后再吞咽。

column3: a. 偶然的, 外来的;偶生的, 偶发的; 异位的
column5: The cuttings developed adventitious roots within weeks of being placed in water.
column6: 插枝放入水中几周内就长出了不定根。

column3: a. 瘟疫的, 有害的, 传播疾病的, 讨厌的, 恼人的;疫病的
column5: The troops avoided the pestilential swamps where fever spread every summer.
column6: 部队避开了那片瘟疫滋生的沼泽,那里每年夏天都流行热病。

column3: vt. 召集...开会
column5: The dean will convoke an emergency meeting to discuss the budget cuts.
column6: 院长将召开紧急会议,讨论预算削减问题。

column3: vt. 议论, 辩驳, 驳击;vi. 参加辩论
column5: No scholar has managed to controvert the evidence in those geological records.
column6: 还没有学者能驳倒那些地质记录中的证据。

column3: a. 无利的, 无益的
column5: After two profitless years, the riverside cafe finally closed its doors.
column6: 连续两年无利可图后,这家河边咖啡馆终于关门了。

column3: vt. 填迟...的日期;n. 事后日期
column5: These letters postdate the treaty, so they cannot describe the original negotiations.
column6: 这些信件写于条约之后,不可能描述当时的谈判。

column3: n. 掺杂, 掺假的东西;掺杂; 掺加
column5: Inspectors fined the firm for the adulteration of olive oil with cheaper seed oils.
column6: 检查员因该公司往橄榄油里掺廉价种子油而开出罚单。

column3: n. 除臭剂, 防臭剂;除臭剂
column5: A simple deodorizer made from baking soda keeps the refrigerator smelling fresh.
column6: 用小苏打做的简易除味剂能让冰箱保持气味清新。

column3: n. 地震学
column5: Advances in seismology help scientists map fault lines beneath crowded cities.
column6: 地震学的进步帮助科学家绘制拥挤城市下方的断层。

column3: n. 生机论, 活力论;生机论, 生活力说
column5: Vitalism lost support once chemists synthesized organic compounds in ordinary laboratories.
column6: 自从化学家在普通实验室里合成有机物,活力论便失去了支持。

column3: n. 辱骂, 毁谤, 耻辱
column5: The mayor endured years of public obloquy after the stadium project failed.
column6: 体育场项目失败后,市长忍受了多年的公开毁谤。

column3: a. 好搞派系的, 好结党营私的
column5: The factious committee split into rival groups and blocked every proposal.
column6: 派系纷争的委员会分裂成对立阵营,否决了一切提案。

column3: a. 无远见的, 浪费的
column5: Improvident spending during the boom years left the city deep in debt.
column6: 繁荣年份的挥霍让这座城市深陷债务。

column3: n. 领带夹
column5: He fastened his silk cravat with a small pearl stickpin.
column6: 他用一枚珍珠领带针别住真丝领结。

column3: a. 人为的, 人工的, 不自然的;人工的, 人造的, 假的
column5: The sudden demand looked factitious, stirred up by dealers hoarding the stamps.
column6: 这股突发的需求看似人为炒作,是商家囤积邮票所致。

column3: n. 小型拨弦古钢琴, 小型立式钢琴
column5: She restored a 1780 spinet and now gives monthly concerts in her parlor.
column6: 她修复了一架1780年的小键琴,如今每月在客厅开音乐会。

column3: n. 咒, 坏话
column5: The old letter contained a malediction against anyone who opened the chest.
column6: 那封旧信里有一道诅咒,针对任何打开箱子的人。

column3: vt. 扰乱, 搅乱, 弄乱
column5: A gust of wind swept through the study and disarranged the papers.
column6: 一阵风穿过书房,弄乱了他桌上的文件。

column3: a. 音响好的, 悦耳的, 声音和谐的
column5: The poet chose euphonious place names for the valleys in her fantasy novel.
column6: 这位诗人为奇幻小说中的山谷取了音韵优美的名字。

column3: a. 不觉痛苦的, 不受伤害的, 无感觉的, 无感情的
column5: The judge remained impassible while the lawyer shouted across the courtroom.
column6: 律师在法庭上大喊大叫,法官始终面无表情。

column3: vt. 诽谤, 中伤, 背叛;诽谤, 中伤, 诋毁
column5: His rivals tried to traduce his reputation with rumors and half-truths.
column6: 对手们企图用谣言和半真半假的话诋毁他的名誉。

column3: n. 轻快, 活泼
column5: She answered each question with briskness, keeping the meeting under thirty minutes.
column6: 她答问干脆利落,把会议控制在三十分钟以内。

column3: n. 悦耳之音
column5: Translators often sacrifice literal accuracy for the euphony of the target language.
column6: 译者常常为了目标语言的音韵美感而舍弃字面对应。

column3: vt. 修订, 校勘
column5: The editor proposed to emend two lines corrupted by centuries of hand copying.
column6: 编校者建议校改这两行因历代手抄而讹误的文字。
